RFC2661-10-1.note: Cleanup clause now proven: TestRFC2661CDNCleansUpAndSendsNothing asserts the session leaves, one session-down, and one kernel teardown for the established case only. Clause 'does not send back any indication' is confounded the same way as RFC2661-9-1: the ICRP is never acknowledged, the cwnd-1 window is full, and a reply handleCDN enqueued would sit in sendQueue with nextSendSeq unchanged and no datagram returned. Negative TestSession_CDN_UnknownSessionDropped is accepted as the 'specific call' scope. Fix: ackAll after setup, or assert sendQueue unchanged.

RFC2661-10-2.note: Sender, both IDs: TestRFC2661LocalIDsNeverZero (see RFC2661-24.10-1). Receiver: TestRFC2661PeerZeroTunnelIDRefused refuses Assigned Tunnel ID 0 and accepts 1 in parseSCCRQ; TestSession_SIDBoundary_Zero/MaxUint16 do the session half.

RFC2661-24.10-1.note: Sender, both IDs: TestRFC2661LocalIDsNeverZero drives allocateLocalTID across the 0xFFFF wrap (the producer skips 0 and tidNoTunnel) and 2^20 allocateSessionID draws, which reach a raw 0 with near certainty; every caller treats the 0 return as exhaustion. Receiver refusal of a peer's zero tunnel ID by SCCRQ and SCCRP units and the .ci. Same text as RFC2661-10-2 (retirement candidate).

RFC2661-24.12-1.note: Session clause: forbidden = escalating a session-scoped unknown M=1 AVP to tunnel teardown, or not terminating the session. session_fsm_test.go::TestSession_UnknownMandatoryAVP asserts the tunnel stays established, but only len(out)==1, not that the message is a CDN nor that the session is removed. Tunnel clause (the second sentence of the quote): no unit tagged with this id.

RFC2661-4.1-1.note: Send clause proven (.ci record, TestAVPCatalogRoundTrip). Receive clause: TestRFC2661ReservedAVPBitTreatedAsUnrecognized is well isolated (the reserved-bit branch in parseICRQ runs before the type switch, and the M=0 case asserts the value 77 was not honored), but it drives ICRQ only. The HELLO path never walks its body (handleMessage returns nil for MsgHello), so a HELLO carrying an M=1 reserved-bit AVP is silently accepted: 'treated as an unrecognized AVP' is unmet there. Blocked by the D-8 fix that owns RFC2661-4.1-4; re-judge after it lands.

RFC2661-4.1-2.note: Positive TestRFC2661EveryEmittedMessageOpensWithMessageType reads the first AVP of all ten body writers plus the HELLO; these are the eleven non-test sites that write a Message Type AVP (SCCRQ, SCCRP, SCCCN, StopCCN, ICRQ, ICRP, ICCN, OCRQ, OCRP, CDN, HELLO). Negative TestReactor_MalformedSCCRQCreatesNoTunnel: an SCCRQ with Host Name first is refused and creates no tunnel. Text duplicates RFC2661-4.4.1-2.

RFC2661-4.1-3.note: Forbidden = keeping a session alive after an unrecognized M=1 AVP in a session message. session_fsm_test.go::TestSession_UnknownMandatoryAVP asserts only len(out)==1 and tunnel still established; it does not assert the one message is a CDN nor that the session is removed, so an implementation that ignored the AVP and answered ICRP would pass. Positive TestSession_IncomingLNS_ICRQ is fine.

RFC2661-4.1-4.note: Forbidden = keeping the tunnel after an unrecognized M=1 AVP in a tunnel message. tunnel_initiator_test.go::TestTunnelSCCCNUnknownMandatoryAVP_StopCCN asserts StopCCN and state Closed, which goes red on that. Clause '(and all sessions within)': the case is an SCCCN before establishment, so no session exists; no tagged unit asserts sessions are cleared for a tunnel-scoped unknown M=1 AVP on an established tunnel.

RFC2661-4.4-1.note: TestRFC2661WrittenAVPFlags compares every AVP of the ten writers to the Section 4.4 M-bit table, and TestRFC2661HelloAVPMandatoryBits closes the one emitted body that walk missed (HELLO). Every Message Type emission site is covered. Single-polarity marker accepted: a sender obligation with no receiver refusal.

RFC2661-4.4-2.note: Forbidden = an M=0-defined AVP (Tie Breaker, the one Ze emits) sent with M=1. message_rfc2661_test.go::TestRFC2661WrittenAVPFlags compares the emitted M bit to rfc2661MandatoryBit (false for Tie Breaker) over the SCCRQ writer that emits it. Row carries single-polarity.

RFC2661-4.4-3.note: Forbidden = an AVP whose definition forbids hiding emitted with H=1. message_rfc2661_test.go::TestRFC2661WrittenAVPFlags walks every AVP of every body Ze writes and fails on any H=1. Row carries single-polarity.

RFC2661-5.8-1.note: TestRFC2661RetransmitBackoffDoubles ticks 1ns before and at 1s, 3s and 7s: a constant 1s interval fires before the 3s deadline and goes red, a missing retransmit goes red. Single-polarity marker accepted.

RFC2661-5.8-2.note: Forbidden = a backoff cap under 8 s. reliable_seq_test.go::TestBackoffCapAtLeast8Seconds asserts DefaultRTimeoutCap>=8s and that newTunnel (the reactor's construction path) yields engine rtimeoutCap>=8s; lowering the constant or the default wiring goes red. Row carries single-polarity.

RFC2661-5.8-3.note: The correction is accepted: the configurability parenthetical is judged under RFC2661-5.8-8. The MUST clause is still half proven. TestTickMaxAttempts proves the engine reports TeardownRequired after the budget and not before; TestPeerTeardownWithdrawsSubscriberRoute's claim says the tunnel is torn down, but its body asserts only one OnSessionDown for the one session. No tagged unit asserts the tunnel state (closed or reaped, StopCCN sent) after exhaustion, so a reactor that withdrew the route and kept the tunnel open stays green.

RFC2661-5.8-4.note: Forbidden = a retransmit carrying the stale Nr, or a new Ns. reliable_test.go::TestTickRetransmit asserts retransmit Nr==1 (updated) and Ns==0 (unchanged); either violation goes red.

RFC2661-5.8-5.note: Forbidden = a duplicate reprocessed, or a duplicate not acknowledged. reliable_test.go::TestOnReceiveDuplicate asserts Class==ClassDuplicate, Delivered empty (ignored from processing) and NeedsZLB true after the piggyback cleared it (MUST be acknowledged). The piggyback/ZLB alternative is permissive.

RFC2661-5.8-6.note: TestRFC2661PeerWindowOfFourAccepted goes through newWindow (and so clampPeerRWS) with peer RWS 4: available(0)==4 and available(3)==1 go red on any clamp below 4; available(4)==0 proves the 'before backing off' half of the sentence's parenthetical. The old negative on TestWindowPeerRWSZero proves the neighbouring RWS=0 rule and is not counted.

RFC2661-5.8-7.note: TestRFC2661ClosedTunnelKeptForRetransmissionInterval drives the reactor's reapExpiredLocked on a StopCCN-closed tunnel built with the reactor's ReliableConfig: kept at 31s-1ns, reaped at 31s. TestPostTeardownAckRetention proves the engine still acknowledges a retransmitted StopCCN during retention, so both 'maintained' and 'operated' are asserted.

RFC2661-6.1-1.note: Sender: TestRFC2661SCCRQCarriesSection61AVPs asserts all five AVPs in writeSCCRQBody with and without the optional AVPs. Receiver: one case per missing AVP answered with StopCCN and no tunnel (unit and .ci), positive with every AVP. The §7.1 clearing now rows as RFC2661-7.1-1.

RFC2661-6.2-1.note: Sender: TestRFC2661SCCRPCarriesSection62AVPs asserts all five AVPs in writeSCCRPBody with and without Challenge/Response. Receiver: TestSCCRPMissingMandatoryAVPTearsTheTunnelDown covers four members, TestRFC2661SCCRPWithoutMessageTypeRefused the fifth with a paired accept. Correction accepted: the state-table 'not acceptable' transition has no sentence.

RFC2661-7.1-1.note: Row text is verbatim §7.1. TestRFC2661InvalidOrMalformedMessageClearsControlConnection proves a Malformed entry and an unknown M=1 Message Type each log a warning and clear the connection (one StopCCN, session gone, tunnel closed), with the unknown M=0 type ignored as the negative; the window is acknowledged first, so the StopCCN count is not confounded. Missing: §7.1 also defines an invalid message as one 'received in an improper sequence (e.g. an SCCCN sent in reply to an SCCRQ)', and the producer does not clear on it: handleSCCCN ignores an SCCCN outside wait-ctl-conn at Debug, although the §7.2.1 table says 'wait-ctl-reply Receive SCCCN Send StopCCN Clean up' and 'established Receive SCCRQ, SCCRP, SCCCN Send StopCCN Clean up'. No unit covers that half.

RFC2661-9-1.note: Clearing clause proven: TestRFC2661StopCCNClearsSessionsSilently and TestSession_StopCCN_CascadeSessions assert zero sessions. Clause '(without sending any explicit call control messages)' is confounded: the setup never acknowledges the first ICRP, so the congestion window (cwnd 1) is full and the second ICRP already waits in sendQueue. A CDN that handleStopCCN enqueued would join sendQueue, leaving nextSendSeq unchanged and out empty, so both assertions stay green. Fix: ackAll before the StopCCN, or assert sendQueue unchanged.

RFC2661-x-1.note: Send clause: TestRFC2661ReservedHeaderBitsSentZero masks every reserved bit of the control header and of all 16 data-header shapes (red on any reserved bit emitted 1); the .ci reads the SCCRP header off the wire. Receive clause: TestRFC2661ReservedHeaderBitsIgnoredOnReceive sets every reserved bit on a control and a data header and asserts ParseMessageHeader returns the identical struct with no error; ParseMessageHeader is the receive entry and no other receive path re-tests the flag word. The wrong single-polarity marker is gone.
